content.title: Irish actor featured on ‘Game of Thrones’ dies at 35 after battle with rare disease
content.text: NewsIrish actor and writer Michael Patrick has died.HBOIrish actor and writer Michael Patrick, best known for his appearance in a season 6 episode of “Game of Thrones,” has died.He was 35 years old. According to Patrick’s social media, he had been battling Motor Neuron Disease. The MND Association describes the disease as one that “rapidly attacks the nerves that control movement so muscles no longer work” and is incurableALS is the most common form of the disease, but Patrick’s family didn’t reveal his exact diagnosis.“Last night, Mick sadly passed away in the Northern Ireland Hospice,” his wife Naomi Sheehan wrote in an Instagram post Wednesday.“He was admitted 10 days ago and was cared for by the incredible team there. He passed peacefully surrounded by family and friends. Words can’t describe how broken-hearted we are.”In his final social media post on Feb. 6, Patrick revealed that his neurologist estimated he had one year left to live.“Still lots to live for and lots planned,” he wrote.Tuberville: People who ‘talk like’ Ilhan Omar ‘should not be able to vote’Vaping now treated like smoking cigarettes under new Alabama lawAlabama’s SNAP candy and soda ban signed into lawPart of long-vacant Birmingham area mall sold ahead of $124 million redevelopmentIn addition to Game of Thrones, Patrick acted in “Blue Lights,” “This Town” and the BBC series “My Left Nut," which he co-wrote based on his teen years, according to IMDb. He was also featured in six episodes of “Blasts from the Past” and four episodes of “The Spectacular,” among many others. His most recent role was in the 2025 German TV movie, “Mordlichter - Tod auf den Färöer Inseln.”“It’s been said more than once that Mick was an inspiration to everyone who was privileged enough to come into contact with him, not just in the past few years during his illness but in every day of his life,” Sheehan wrote. “He lived a life as full as any human can live. Joy, abundance of spirit, infectious laughter. A titan of a ginger haired man. We are so grateful for every person who supported us through the last few years.”Sheehan went on to highlight a quote Patrick “loved” from Irish writer and activist Brendan Behan. “This feels appropriate now: ‘The most important things to do in the world are to get something to eat, something to drink and somebody to love you.’ So, don’t overthink it. Eat. Drink. Love,” Sheehan concluded, signing the post, “Naomi - Mick’s wife.”Heather Gann is a breaking news and Birmingham metro reporter for AL.com.
